problemStatement: Weekly Radar currently acquires and renders the report, publishes to Telegram, and only then writes the durable archive. A process or network failure during delivery can therefore leave no durable pre-render input for an exact retry, while write_run can overwrite a same-date archive and performs retention before the final write succeeds. The runtime needs a durable immutable input snapshot before rendering, an explicit delivery-only retry path, atomic archive writes, same-date conflict protection, and retention only after a successful archive commit.
outOfScope: Adding Stage, Score, Rank, Top5, investment conclusions, LLM extraction, or trading decisions
Changing source authority semantics or the strict Candidate boundary
Real external Telegram, SEC, GitHub, or production data-branch operations in tests
Changing main branch history or unrelated Work Items

acceptance: The runtime implements Compute → Persist Snapshot → Render → Publish → Archive for normal non-dry runs.
The persisted input snapshot is a complete, versioned, deterministic JSON envelope and is idempotent for identical bytes but rejects same-date conflicting input.
The CLI supports --retry-as-of to render and publish from a persisted input snapshot without external acquisition, and rejects incompatible option combinations.
Archive final files are written atomically, same-date final runs are rejected without mutation, and retention occurs only after all final files and the manifest commit successfully.
Focused unit, integration, CLI, and E2E tests cover ordering, exact retry input, conflict protection, atomic behavior, retention timing, and existing boundaries.
Operational documentation describes the persisted input, retry command, same-date immutability, and failure recovery behavior without exposing secrets.
The AI Change Summary records changed files, verification evidence, guideline compliance, residual risks, unknowns, and complete lifecycle evidence.

intent.problem: The current Weekly Radar path does not make the computed report input durable before delivery and can overwrite an existing date archive. This weakens recovery after partial delivery and makes historical data mutable.
constraints: Keep the runtime deterministic, rule-only, evidence-first, and free of Stage/Score/Rank/Top5 or investment decisions.
Use the existing RuntimeReportInput serialization boundary and current report/receipt identity rather than introducing a new domain model or dependency.
Protect the literal data-branch archive boundary, avoid external live calls in tests, and preserve existing dry-run behavior.

The user authorizes repository changes, local validation, governed evidence writes, PR creation, hosted checks, merge, and Work Item close; no provider-side effect or provider-owned value is authorized.
intent.rationale: Persisting the already-computed runtime input before rendering gives delivery a stable recovery point without changing fact semantics. Atomic writes and pre-mutation same-date checks make the archive append-only by date and keep retention from deleting evidence when a commit fails.

guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Keep persistence and archive errors explicit and do not expose secret-bearing filesystem details.
Do not hand-edit generated current_status.md; regenerate it through Make targets.
Do not weaken the data-branch guard or replace deterministic tests with live external calls.
